text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Motorists who commit traffic offences two weeks before Chinese Lunar New Year and the Moslem Id al-Fitr (in mid-February) will be slapped with the maximum compound fine of 300 ringgit, the Malaysian Cabinet has decided.
-- Road safety campaigns and stiffer penalties have failed to reduce the number of fatal accidents last year, Deputy Transport Minister Mohd Ali Rustam said.
-- A Malaysian diplomat, believed to be attached to Malaysian High Commission in Brunei, was detained at the airport on suspicion of possession of cannabis.
-- A pilot programme for single-session schools is scheduled to begin on June 9 involving 50 institutions, said deputy Education Minister Khalid Yunus.
-- Utility firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd plans to raise US$1 billion in local and foreign markets in the first quarter of the year for part of its capital expenditure,
